items.title: Crimean Bridge damage reported as rail and road traffic suspended
items.summary: Russia's transport authorities reportedly suspended both train and vehicle traffic across the Crimean Bridge while specialists assessed damage following an alleged Ukrainian strike. Images circulating online appear to show a collapsed section, but the extent of structural damage remains unverified; preliminary information indicated no casualties.

items.title: Russian security service alleges disruption of planned coordinated attacks
items.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service says it thwarted a purported Ukrainian-backed plot for simultaneous attacks inside Russia, alleging the seizure of more than 700 kilograms of explosives, at least 40 drones and six jet skis. The allegations, including the claimed Ukrainian intelligence involvement and quantities seized, have not been independently verified.

items.title: Russia alleges overnight strikes hit Ukrainian drone and aircraft-engine plants
items.summary: Russian military statements allege that overnight strikes hit two Kyiv facilities involved in attack-drone production, Techno-Links and Ukrplastic, as well as the Motor Sich and Ivchenko-Progress aircraft-engine plants in Zaporizhzhia. The reported hits, facilities' military roles and extent of any damage have not been independently verified.

items.title: Ukraine says North Korea supplies Russia with dozens of ballistic missiles monthly
items.summary: Ukraine's president says North Korea is supplying Russia with dozens of ballistic missiles each month, allowing Pyongyang to refine its weapons through use in the war. He called for Ukraine to receive comparable capabilities to counter the threat. The stated delivery rate has not been independently verified.

items.title: Ukraine details multi-weapon operation against Crimean Bridge
items.summary: Ukraine's president has claimed responsibility for the latest strikes on the Crimean Bridge, describing weeks of preparatory attacks on air defences and electronic-warfare systems. He said Ukrainian forces used Neptune and FP-5 Flamingo missiles alongside Palyanytsia and Ruta weapons against road and railway sections. Reports of collapsed spans and an arch remain unverified, as does the full extent of damage.

items.title: Emergency electricity outages affect multiple Ukrainian regions
items.summary: Electricity disruptions were reported across several Ukrainian regions, including Odesa, Mykolaiv, Dnipropetrovsk, Rivne, Sumy, Chernihiv and Chernivtsi. Emergency shutdowns were reportedly introduced in Kirovohrad, Poltava and Sumy regions following significant equipment damage. The precise causes, scale and expected restoration times have not been independently confirmed.

items.title: Russia opens investigation and warns against travel to Crimean Bridge
items.summary: Russian authorities have reportedly opened a terrorism investigation into the November 16–17 attacks on the Crimean Bridge and urged motorists to avoid approaching the crossing. Officials say security will be increased along the overland route to Crimea and maintain that supplies remain intact, while the Kremlin has pledged to rebuild the damaged bridge. The full extent of structural damage and the reliability of alternative supply routes remain unverified.

items.title: Hungary reportedly suspends rail services to Ukraine for two days
items.summary: Rail traffic between Hungary and Ukraine is reportedly being suspended for November 17–18 after a drone landed about 300 metres from a station in Mukachevo. The incident reportedly prompted the evacuation of a Hungarian train crew; the drone's origin and whether anyone was injured remain unclear.

items.title: Kyiv sets up additional emergency heating centres amid energy disruptions
items.summary: Local authorities in Kyiv are reportedly installing emergency heating centres in the Troieshchyna district as the city continues to face energy disruptions. Portable sanitation facilities are also planned, although the number of operational centres and their capacity have not been confirmed.

items.title: Kyiv's Southern Bridge reportedly reopens partially after strikes
items.summary: Traffic on Kyiv's Southern Bridge has reportedly resumed in one direction, from the left bank to the right, with vehicle-weight and spacing restrictions. The opposite direction reportedly remains closed because of damage, while the Northern Bridge is also said to have sustained damage. The extent of both bridges' structural damage has not been independently confirmed.

items.title: French military training mission inside Ukraine draws political scrutiny
items.summary: A reported French mission known as Volia has allegedly placed small teams of military instructors inside Ukraine to train personnel and maintain French-supplied weapons, including Caesar artillery and Mirage aircraft. The account has prompted a French opposition politician to demand parliamentary scrutiny and an end to the deployment; the mission's scope and legal status remain disputed.

items.title: Finnish president urges direct European talks with Putin
items.summary: Finnish President Alexander Stubb reportedly called for European leaders to engage directly with Vladimir Putin rather than leave negotiations over the war to other powers. He warned that Europe risks being excluded from decisions affecting its security and argued that any eventual agreement would require Russia's participation.

items.title: Ukraine proposes swapping future Patriot interceptors for immediate supplies
items.summary: Ukraine's president has proposed that NATO partners transfer Patriot air-defence interceptor missiles from existing stockpiles now, with Ukraine replacing them using missiles it has already ordered once they are manufactured. The proposal aims to address an immediate shortage while new interceptors remain subject to lengthy production queues; no agreement was announced.

items.title: France acknowledges limited military personnel presence in Ukraine
items.summary: A French defence official has acknowledged a small French military presence in Ukraine involving coordination, training and equipment support, while maintaining that France is not participating in combat. The statement adds official clarification to earlier accounts of a French training and maintenance mission; its full size and arrangements remain undisclosed.

items.title: Russia says it struck four Ukrainian electricity substations
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry says its forces attacked electricity substations in Rivne, Hrabiv, Kamianske and Chernivtsi, including facilities serving western and central Ukrainian regions. The reported strikes could add pressure to Ukraine's power system, but the damage, civilian impact and operational status of the facilities have not been independently verified.

items.title: Moldova confirms drone airspace violation over Chisinau
items.summary: Moldova's Defence Ministry reportedly confirmed that a drone entered the country's airspace, with a suspected Russian Gerbera-type drone observed over the capital, Chisinau. The aircraft's origin, flight path and purpose have not been independently established, but the incident raises renewed concerns about spillover from the war in neighbouring Ukraine.

items.title: Russia warns French military personnel in Ukraine could be targeted
items.summary: Russia's embassy in France warned that French military personnel deployed to Ukraine could be treated as military targets, describing their presence as an escalation. France has acknowledged a limited training and equipment-support presence while denying participation in combat; the competing positions raise concerns about a broader confrontation.

items.title: US defence official questions effectiveness of Ukrainian long-range strikes
items.summary: US Under Secretary of Defense for Policy Elbridge Colby reportedly told Ukraine's supporters in Brussels that deep strikes inside Russia have not significantly slowed Russian advances or brought the war closer to an end. He also suggested such attacks may strengthen Russian public resolve; the assessment is attributed to his reported remarks and has not been independently corroborated.

items.title: Russia alleges strikes on military cargo ship and railway locomotive in Ukraine
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry says its drones struck a cargo ship allegedly transporting military supplies toward Odesa and a locomotive near Kryvyi Rih reportedly used for military logistics. The identity of the ship, the cargo, the damage and any casualties have not been independently confirmed.

items.title: UK announces £240 million military aid package for Ukraine
items.summary: Britain's defence minister has reportedly announced an additional £240 million in military assistance for Ukraine, including more than 1,000 short-range air-defence missiles, launch systems and over a dozen air-defence radars. Deliveries are expected to begin in December; the precise equipment types and delivery schedule have not been independently confirmed.

items.title: Moldova says seven drones entered its airspace, with five reportedly downed
items.summary: Moldova's Defence Ministry reportedly identified seven drones over the country, with five said to have fallen near settlements and two still unlocated. Airports and all six crossings on the Ukrainian border were reportedly temporarily suspended. The drones' origins and the circumstances of their flights have not been independently confirmed.

items.title: Putin reportedly arrives in Shenzhen for APEC summit and high-level talks
items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin reportedly arrived in Shenzhen for the APEC summit, with meetings involving Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump on the agenda, including a reported three-way meeting. The content and outcome of any talks concerning Ukraine remain unknown.

items.title: Ukraine seeks additional €8 billion in military funding and 40 F-16 fighters
items.summary: During a video address to a meeting of Ukraine's Western military supporters in Brussels, President Volodymyr Zelensky reportedly requested another €8 billion this year to address military budget needs, alongside funding for drone production and 40 additional F-16 fighter jets. He also sought Mirage aircraft and air-defence interceptors from European stockpiles. The requests have not been confirmed as new aid commitments.

items.title: NATO says efforts underway to restore Ukraine's access to Starshield
items.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte reportedly said relevant parties are working to restore Ukraine's full access to Starshield, but offered no timetable and did not identify who imposed the restrictions. The nature and extent of the reported access disruption remain unclear, and the account has not been independently confirmed.

items.title: Dutch missile maker reportedly confirms RUTA strikes on Crimean Bridge
items.summary: Netherlands-based weapons manufacturer Destinus reportedly acknowledged that its RUTA cruise missiles were used in strikes on the Crimean Bridge on two consecutive days. The account also alleges Dutch funding for roughly 700 RUTA missiles, but the company's statement, procurement figure and extent of bridge damage have not been independently verified.
